articles.title: Police picked him up at 10 for walking home alone. At 21, he says free-range parenting gave him freedom.
articles.summary: Garrard Conley was enrolled in the now defunct Love in Action conversion therapy program in Memphis, Tennessee, at age 19. He was sent there by his parents after a classmate disclosed his sexual orientation to them following an assault. Conley grew up in a deeply religious family in rural Arkansas. He says he had to attend the program or face rejection from his family, and he ultimately agreed to enter the program. Conley talks to Business Insider about the long-term harms of the practice, how it remains legal in much of the US, and how a new Supreme Court case threatens to strip away the few protections that currently exist. In 2016, years after leaving the program, Conley published a memoir titled "Boy Erased," which was later adapted into a film. He's since reconciled with his parents and has dedicated much of his work to educating the public on the dangers of conversion therapy. His educational podcast, "Unerased," traces the history of the conversion therapy movement. The final episode features John Smid, the former director of Love in Action, who has since disavowed the practice and come out as gay.
articles.body:
Bundled in heavy coats, hats, scarves, and mittens, Rafi Meitiv and his little sister Dvora had just spent a sunny Saturday afternoon in December 2014 playing at a local playground in suburban Maryland.

After an hour, the 10- and 6-year-olds began their trek home , about three-quarters of a mile. While it was their first time walking from that particular park to their house alone, they'd traced the same route in Silver Spring dozens of times with their parents and had also ventured off alone to other playgrounds in the area before.

About halfway through their journey, they were stopped by three police officers, who instructed them to get in their car so they could drive them home and speak to their parents.

"At this point, we knew how to obviously use crosswalks, walk the street safely," Rafi, now 21, told Business Insider in his first time speaking out about this incident in over a decade. "We had our parents' phone numbers. We knew how to take care of ourselves."

The incident led to a six-month investigation into potential child neglect by Child Protective Services , followed by another, more harrowing run-in with CPS and the police.

Rafi and Dvora's parents, Alexander and Danielle Meitiv, fought back, appearing on TV news programs, including "Today" and "Good Morning America." They were eventually cleared of "unsubstantiated child abuse or neglect" — a legal limbo meaning that CPS could neither find enough evidence to prove nor fully rule out neglect — in June 2015.

The Maryland Department of Human Services told Business Insider in a comment that it's "committed to transparency and being as open as possible while maintaining the confidentiality of children and their families, as protected by law."

The Meitivs' story isn't unique. In August 2026, Karyann Parkinson , a mom of five from Virginia, was convicted of "contributing to the delinquency of a minor" after allowing her 5-year-old son to walk half a mile alone within their gated community. It earned her a six-month prison sentence, which was immediately suspended, and landed her on the state's child abuse and neglect registry for seven years, banning her from volunteering at her children's schools, among other things. The Parkinsons have since left their HOA and filed an appeal, hoping to have their case heard before a jury.

Parkinson's case recently reignited the debate around childhood independence in the US. For parents who are mindfully raising free-range kids, the decision to let their kid walk or play alone comes with risks. Besides considering the obvious ones — like their children getting hurt or lost — parents may also worry about being slapped with a child-neglect investigation or criminally prosecuted for endangering the welfare of a child.

Rafi said he loved being a free-range kid because it taught him to be more "street-smart" and gave him the freedom to roam around, climbing trees and jumping into streams. "It was definitely better than being inside on an iPad for my entire childhood," he said.

The drawbacks were his brushes with the system designed to protect him.

"I was definitely having nightmares during the whole ordeal and afterward," he said. "It was just not something a kid should have to go through."

CPS visits at school and a 'safety plan'

When the police arrived at the Meitivs' home with Rafi and Dvora in the backseat, the atmosphere quickly became "extremely hostile and intimidating," Rafi later wrote in his college application essay to Towson University, where he's now studying exercise science .

Alexander Meitiv, now 55, was the only one home because his wife, Danielle, now 57, was on a work trip. When the father of two opened the door, he was told he needed to show ID before his children could be let in. At one point, Rafi called his mom and said he was afraid "Daddy is going to be arrested."

Alexander was given a "safety plan" to sign, which involved two instructions: "The children will not be left unsupervised by an adult anywhere," and that Alexander would "avail himself" to CPS while it investigated the incident. There was no clear end date to the restrictions.

After that night, CPS began investigating the Meitivs for potential child neglect. At one point, Rafi and Dvora were pulled out of their classrooms in their nearby school to be interviewed by a CPS worker.

"They were asking serious questions, 'Do your parents hurt you?'" Rafi said. "I was just shocked."

According to Rafi, Danielle only learned about the questioning when she was interviewed by the same CPS employee later that day, who had a school-visitation sticker.

Two months after their children's run-in with police, the Meitivs received a letter from CPS saying they had been found responsible for "unsubstantiated child abuse or neglect." While not an official ruling, it would remain on file for the next five years.

"I might laugh about that now — what does that mean, 'unsubstantiated'?" Danielle told Business Insider. "But I remember crying. I can't believe they think they were neglecting our children. I pride myself on really caring, being so deliberate in my parenting."

Reflecting on his past, Rafi said he didn't feel unsafe because of his free-range childhood . If he ever got lost, for example, he said he felt confident he could approach a security guard and recite his parents' phone number from memory.

His free-range lifestyle came with limitations, too. "We weren't allowed to go across big streets. We weren't always unsupervised in other areas," he said. "It was mainly just that they would let us go for walks."

Tighter fences around free-range parenting

Many American parents long for their kids to experience more of the "latchkey" childhoods they themselves enjoyed. Still, they hesitate to actually implement that level of independence.

A 2023 poll from the University of Michigan's C.S. Mott Children's Hospital, surveying 2,044 parents in the US, found that 84% of parents of 9- to 11-year-olds agreed that kids benefit from time without adult supervision. Yet only 33% said their child had walked or biked alone to a friend's house, 15% said their child had trick-or-treated with friends, and 58% said their child had stayed home alone for 30 to 60 minutes.

A common parental fear — the risk of kids being kidnapped while venturing alone — is rare. A 2026 report from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children found that non-family abductions make up only 1% of all reported missing-child cases in the US.

Lenore Skenazy, president of Let Grow , a nonprofit promoting childhood independence, told Business Insider that parents and bystanders have been culturally convinced that responsible parenting means hypervigilance.

"I call it 'worst-first thinking,' Skenazy said. She cited milk cartons of missing children in the 1980s, the "Taken" franchise, and nearly three decades of "Law and Order: SVU" as contributing to parental anxiety around kidnappings, homicides, and sexual abuse against minors. It's "jumping to the worst-case scenario first and proceeding as if it's likely to happen."

She added that both parents and kids benefit from gradually releasing the reins . "When you let go, and you see what your kid can do on their own, that rewires a parent like nothing else," Skenazy said. "You've gone from, 'My kid is a baby, they need me, they'll be hurt, and I'll feel terrible forever,' to 'Look at what my kid can do, how beautifully they're growing up.'"

The question is not whether children should gain independence, pediatric safety experts say, but how much freedom is appropriate for a child's age, skills, and surroundings. The American Academy of Pediatrics notes that most children are not ready to cross streets alone until at least age 10, and has called for communities to make routes to school and play safer so children can move about independently.

"You have to take into consideration not only your personal children, but also geography," Sheri Langston, a licensed professional counselor practicing in Colorado and California who focuses on families, told Business Insider. "Every parent gets to make those decisions, those choices: 'What am I OK exposing my children to?'"

As a free-range kid, Rafi said he sympathizes with fearful parents, but added that it shouldn't hold them back from letting their children have more autonomy . "The benefits of letting your kids have some independence and walk around the neighborhood far outweigh the negatives," he continued.

In the months following the February 2015 letter from CPS, Rafi felt things had blown over — the family hadn't heard from CPS again. The Meitivs resumed letting their kids walk home alone. As a precaution, they gave Rafi and Dvora laminated " kid licenses " to hand to strangers in case they were stopped.

In April 2015, Rafi and Dvora stopped to pet a stranger's dog on their way home. When they kept walking, they noticed the man following them. Eventually, he called the police. This time, the children weren't driven home. Instead, they waited for hours in the back of a police car. All the while, they wondered if they'd be separated from their parents this time.

Rafi said his parents weren't notified for hours and had begun searching the neighborhood for them. Eventually, they realized their children must have been picked up by the police again.

When they arrived at CPS headquarters around 8:30 p.m. with food for the kids, Rafi said, it took an additional two hours for the family to be reunited.

After their second and more serious interaction with CPS, the Meitivs signed the new safety plan, which would now also require them to escort the kids to and from school .

After two appeals, CPS dropped its investigation in June 2015. That same month, Maryland's Department of Human Resources issued guidance saying that CPS should not investigate cases involving children walking or playing outside alone unless the children were harmed or were in substantial risk of harm. Maryland state law also prohibits leaving a child under 8 alone in a home, building enclosure, or car without a reliable person over 13 present.

In May 2026, Congress introduced a bill titled "Promoting Childhood Independence and Resilience Act of 2026," which would cover activities like kids walking or biking alone , running errands, taking public transit, and staying home alone for brief periods of time, so long as they don't present "unreasonable disregard of a foreseeable risk of serious harm." Movement on the bill has been slow, and if it dies with this Congress, it would need to be reintroduced in 2027.

Rafi sees a direct link between how he was raised and who he's become as an adult.

"I have a lot of friends at school right now who had a much more helicopter-ed, for lack of a better word, childhood, and they are a lot less independent," he said. "They have to call their parents for every decision that they make."

Comparatively, he said he feels more comfortable navigating unfamiliar places and interacting with strangers. He also just remembers having more fun.

"I look back at my childhood and the freedom I had," Rafi said. "It felt like being a kid the way it's supposed to be."

If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

articles.title: The “Locking In” Trend Is All About Taking Back Control of Your Life—Here’s How to Try It
articles.summary: The 5 a.m. alarms are really about something else.
articles.body:
"Locking in" means going all-in on your goals with strict, streak-based challenges like 75 Hard or Winter Arc.

Fall feels like a natural fresh start, and experts say that "chapter break" feeling can make change seem more doable. Starting a challenge now can also help people get ahead of the winter months, when mental health is most vulnerable.

The all-or-nothing approach has a catch: One missed day can feel like total failure. It may not suit people who are burned out or prone to perfectionism, disordered eating, or rigid thinking.

If your FYP looks anything like mine right now, everyone is "locking in." People are setting 5 a.m. alarms, cutting out sugar, doing no-spend days and dry months, and reading 10 pages a day, often all at once.

Some call it 75 Hard , some call it their Winter Arc , but the premise is the same: For a couple of months, go all-in on your goals without missing a day, and you'll come out on the other side a whole new person.

It sounds intense, and honestly, not very fun. But as someone who's always " in a rut ," I can see the need to take such drastic measures. October is already here, and I still haven't accomplished all the things I'd set out to do for the year. Maybe it really is time for 75 Hard.

Judging by my FYP, I'm not the only one. So what does our obsession with "locking in" say about us, and is it actually doing us any good?

Why Control Is What We're Really Craving

I'm burned out . I have my 9-to-5, side hustles, fitness routine, creative projects, and to worry about. Other 20- and 30-somethings similarly have a lot on their plate. And as much as I like to think of it as highly ambitious behavior, perhaps being overloaded makes us feel a little out of control.

Gary Dillon , a licensed psychologist and founder of Ally Psychological Therapy, explains that pursuing lock-in challenges all boils down to control. "Many people are managing economic crises, , feelings of being overwhelmed, and pressure to manage it all and still do more," he says. "So highly structured challenges become the shield and sword against the battle of uncertainty and lack of control."

Kimberly Fishbach, a clinical psychologist at Soho Integrative Psychological Services says all-or-nothing thinking has evolutionary roots. "This mindset has allowed humans to quickly make decisions when survival depended on it," she says. Challenges like 75 Hard and Winter Arc remove "the psychological resistance, time, and effort that otherwise might accompany the daunting task of changing an ingrained behavior," she adds. "It creates less time to talk ourselves out of doing what feels hard."

There's another reason we love these trends: Humans love a good story. Just think about how big the concept of "being the main character " was a few years ago. Or "doing it for the plot." We all yearn to tell the tale, even if it's just to ourselves.

"With trends like 75 Hard and Winter Arc, we get to be the writer and star of our own story, and who doesn't want to be Rocky or the Karate Kid?" Dillon says.

and cooling temperatures make fall feel like a for many. It makes sense that the season is a popular time for "locking in," and Katy Milkman , a professor at The Wharton School and author of How to Change , notes that the start of the new school year adds to this energy.

"Picking moments that feel like fresh starts or chapter breaks can help us feel separated from past failures ('that misstep was the old me last year/season') and more capable of making a change," she says. Fall is also the beginning of 4:30 p.m. sunsets. Doing a lock-in challenge can help people get ahead "in anticipation of the winter season, when is most susceptible to declining," Fishbach says.

Structure Is Effective, But There's a Catch

From the looks of it, 75 Hard and Winter Arc are effective. I've seen countless videos of people posting their fitness transformations, reflecting on how motivated they feel, and pointing to how grit has made them all-the-more tenacious.

However, structure is great until it isn't. With the extremity of lock-in trends, breaking a streak can seem like a way bigger mistake than it actually is. "The goal should not be to practice perfectionism in the context of a perfect streak; it should be to give ourselves permission to return to the structured habit after the streak has been discontinued," Dillon says. "I challenge my client to lean into observations and away from judgments. 'I couldn't continue my streak today' is an observation of what happened,' [instead of] 'I'm a failure because I couldn't continue my streak.' Now that's the sort of judgment we hope to avoid. This small shift often helps them avoid believing that one slip-up has doomed it all."

For those of us who already feel burned out, locking in might not be the best way to approach our goals. If we're already stretched thin, why would we add more to our plate?

"The irony is that many are in this intersection of burnout and optimization," Dillon says. We're all tracking steps, sleep, and habits as a way to maintain control, "but control is not healing, and those of us who are experiencing burnout don't need more challenge or a demanding routine; we need rest, comfort, safety, and permission to stop performing," Dillon says.

He also warns that locking in isn't for everyone. "Anyone who has or is currently struggling with perfectionism, disordered eating, moderate anxiety, obsessive or rigid thinking, or compulsive behavior should be mindful of the rigidity of the challenges and how they might be triggered," he says. "Additionally, high-achieving folks should be cautious, as they tend to be very good at creating performance metrics for self-care."

Milkman emphasizes the importance of building habits in a way that you enjoy. "If it's drudgery, you won't stick to it." she says. On that note, I'll be looking into 75 Soft —75 Hard's mellowed out sister.

articles.title: Chose dark, CCTV-free cellar: How ex-guard planned 5-year-old’s murder for quick money
articles.summary: Hyderabad police arrested ex-Orchid Villas guard Vikram Kumar for a 5-year-old’s murder, alleging he used a dark, CCTV-free cellar and sought ransom.
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Over 24 hours after the ghastly murder of a five-year-old girl at Villa Orchids in Kowkoor, Bollaram police arrested the prime accused Vikram Kumar, a former security guard of the housing society late on Sunday night.Cops said that the accused spent less than 25 minutes inside the gated community to carry out the crime, deliberately choosing a secluded, dark spot in the clubhouse cellar with no CCTV coverage.“Vikram confessed to have killed the girl to make quick money. He made her his target as he knew she stepped out to play in the evenings and that her family, which maintained a low profile, could afford to pay a ransom,” Malkajgiri police commissioner, B Sumathi, said while announcing his arrest.A native of Nalanda in Bihar, Vikram had joined the society’s security staff four months ago. He was fired just a day before the crime for poor conduct.Police said that the accused kept an eye on the girl, who had gone into the clubhouse to watch Bathukamma celebrations, and allegedly lured her to the under-construction cellar within the property, soon after she stepped out -- under some unknown pretext. Since the minor was acquainted to Vikram, she didn’t hesitate to follow him.Once in the cellar, he allegedly used construction material lying around to strangle her to death. He then tied her hands and legs, fastened bricks to her body and drowned her in a water sump, the commissioner added.Immediately afterwards, Vikram exited the gated community through the main gate and called the minor’s family to demand a ransom. He had retrieved their numbers from the register kept at the society’s main gate.While both the child’s father and grandfather, who the accused spoke to, agreed to pay the ransom of Rs 20 lakh on condition that Vikram first make a WhatsApp video call to prove that the girl was alive, he refused to do so.They family lodged a police complaint at around 9.45 pm on Saturday.“For the first four hours after receiving the complaint, we checked footage from 130 CCTV cameras to locate the minor girl. Simultaneously searches were also conducted at Secunderabad railway station and other places to trace the accused, based on his mobile tower location,” Sumathi said.After reviewing the investigation, at around 2 am on Sunday, police decided to search within the gated community, focusing on secluded parts of the campus. “That is when our team eventually found the girl’s body in the cellar, a spot that residents rarely visited,” she added.Incidentally, residents of the community told police, Vikram had been caught smoking and drinking in the cellar just a few days earlier. When the matter came to the notice of his security agency, he was dismissed from his job.“Meanwhile, after committing the crime, Vikram returned to his room in Kowkoor that he shared with other employees of the security agency. He later travelled using different modes of transport, including an autorickshaw, and reached Patancheru, where he was apprehended from late on Sunday night,” said the police commissioner.After securing his judicial remand, police said they will seek custody of the accused for further interrogation. “We are also waiting for information from Nalanda police to verify Vikram’s antecedents,” Sumathi added.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: More people seen entering and exiting NYC manholes: What to know
articles.summary: The latest incident occurred in the Hamilton Heights neighborhood of Manhattan.
articles.body:
Multiple people were seen dropping into a Manhattan manhole early Sunday morning, according to police, marking yet another incident in recent weeks involving people entering or exiting manholes across New York City.

Police are searching for three men seen entering a manhole on West 141st Street, in New York City's Hamilton Heights neighborhood, shortly before 1 a.m. on Sunday, New York Police Department sources told ABC News.

By the time police arrived, the men were gone, the sources said.

The manhole incident follows a separate incident just days earlier on Oct. 9, when police say four men and a woman were spotted emerging from a manhole on Manhattan's Upper East Side. The group drove away in a black SUV and left behind shovels and other tools, according to police sources.

Police believe these urban scavengers pose no threat and instead are looking for valuables dropped or swept away after it rains.

The events over the weekend follow similar recent instances of individuals seen entering or exiting the manholes found across New York City streets.

Last month, in a separate incident, police arrested two individuals in connection with a sighting of people climbing out of a manhole near a hotel where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stayed briefly during the U.N. General Assembly in September.

The NYPD and federal agents conducted additional sweeps of the area out of an abundance of caution given the U.N. General Assembly and the proximity to Netanyahu's hotel, but nothing suspicious was found.

The same week, on Friday, Sept. 25, police said three men were spotted climbing out of the sewer at Bay Ridge Parkway and 17th Avenue in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, at 4:34 a.m.

The manhole was closed by the time police arrived.

articles.summary: Segundo a Polícia Federal, Paula Simões e Patrick Cardoso assumiram as operações criminosas após a prisão de integrantes da 'Ndrangheta', em 2019.
articles.body:
O Fantástico deste domingo (11) mostrou que uma investigação conjunta das polícias do Brasil e da Itália r evelou um esquema milionário de tráfico internacional de drogas ligado à 'Ndrangheta', uma das principais organizações mafiosas italianas.

Entre os suspeitos de comandar o envio de cocaína para a Europa a partir de portos brasileiros estão a influenciadora digital Paula Simões e o advogado Patrick Cardoso , presos durante a operação.

Conhecida por compartilhar vídeos de sua rotina nas redes sociais, Paula é suspeita de ter assumido os negócios da máfia italiana no Brasil após a prisão do marido, Patrick Assisi, em 2019. Ele e o pai, Nicola Assisi, integrantes da organização criminosa, foram encontrados escondidos em Praia Grande, no litoral de São Paulo.

A ascensão da influenciadora chamou a atenção dos investigadores porque, tradicionalmente, as mulheres não costumam ocupar posições de liderança na 'Ndrangheta'.

"Pelas próprias regras da máfia, normalmente, a mulher não tem tanto protagonismo. Mas nesse caso, sim", afirmou o delegado Eduardo Verza.

Segundo a investigação, Paula teria contado com a ajuda do advogado Patrick Cardoso, que defendia os mafiosos presos e atuaria como intermediário entre eles e os integrantes da organização em liberdade.

Paula Simões é suspeita de assumir o comando de esquema de tráfico internacional de drogas — Foto: Reprodução/Fantástico

Segundo a Polícia Federal, o grupo utilizava a estrutura logística do Porto de Paranaguá, no Paraná, para enviar grandes quantidades de cocaína à Europa, escondidas em contêineres. Doleiros também eram usados para movimentar o dinheiro do tráfico.

Mesmo após a prisão de Nicola e Patrick Assisi, a organização teria continuado operando. De acordo com os investigadores, o advogado Patrick Cardoso se aproveitava do contato reservado com os clientes presos para transmitir orientações sobre os negócios criminosos.

"A esposa de um desses mafiosos trocava muitas mensagens com um advogado, que era quem os representava quando foram presos, tratando sobre fornecedores de droga, pagamento de dívidas. E conversas ali com um indicativo muito forte de atuação do narcotráfico internacional", afirmou o delegado Eduardo Verza.

A polícia encontrou fotografias de bilhetes produzidos dentro da Superintendência da PF em São Paulo. Neles, os mafiosos davam ordens sobre os negócios da organização, incluindo a cobrança de dívidas. Em uma das cartas, Patrick Assisi orientava Paula a enviar um comparsa conhecido como "BXX" para recuperar dinheiro e bens que pudessem ser vendidos.

O depoimento de um integrante da própria 'Ndrangheta', na Itália, também ajudou os investigadores a identificar uma nova liderança da organização no Brasil.

Patrick Cardoso e Paula Simões, presos em operação sobre esquema internacional de drogas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo a investigação, quando Paula e o advogado passaram a atuar à frente das operações, o grupo tinha mais de duas toneladas de cocaína em estoque.

Em conversas obtidas pela polícia, Paula aparece negociando o envio de 400 quilos de cocaína para a Europa. As mensagens, trocadas em italiano por meio de um aplicativo utilizado por criminosos, mostram uma negociação sobre preço, qualidade da droga e transporte até Paranaguá.

Traficante: "Qual é o preço do seu material?"

Paula: "Eu vou tirar fotos esta semana, ok?"

Traficante: "É importante que seja top."

Paula: "Porém, para mandar para Paranaguá, com o frete, fica 5150, ok?"

Para a polícia, as mensagens deixam claro que Paula e Eduardo eram os representantes dos Assisi fora da cadeia.

A defesa de Patrick Cardoso afirmou que o advogado sempre atuou dentro dos limites da advocacia ao longo de 25 anos de carreira e que já apresentou um pedido de revogação da prisão preventiva.

O advogado de Paula Simões afirmou que ela nega todas as acusações e que nenhuma droga foi apreendida com ela. Segundo a defesa, a suspeita de que as atividades criminosas teriam continuado após a prisão dos Assisi são inferências da autoridade policial, não fatos comprovados.

Segundo a polícia, o grupo comandado pelos mafiosos liderava um esquema de tráfico internacional de drogas que movimentou quantias incalculáveis de dinheiro.

articles.title: Edital Social do Sicoob realiza sonho de instituição beneficente em Itaperuna | G1
articles.standfirst: Creche Menino Jesus, que atende mais de 200 crianças, ganha novo playground.
articles.summary: Creche Menino Jesus, que atende mais de 200 crianças, ganha novo playground.
articles.body:
A responsabilidade social pode ganhar muitas formas. Às vezes, ela cabe em uma casinha, passa por um escorrega e termina no sorriso de uma criança. Em Itaperuna, no Noroeste Fluminense, uma iniciativa do Sicoob viabilizou um playground para a Creche Menino Jesus, que atende mais de 200 crianças, de um a cinco anos de idade. A estrutura realiza um antigo sonho da instituição beneficente que, há mais de 40 anos, acolhe pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade social.

Padre Geraldo Gualandi, de 75 anos, fundador da creche — Foto: Divulgação

A modernização da área de lazer das crianças foi possível graças ao Edital Social, projeto criado para apoiar organizações da sociedade civil sem fins lucrativos que integra a estratégia de responsabilidade social do sistema regional Sicoob ES. A iniciativa, que está em sua 8ª edição, apoia projetos que tenham como foco áreas como educação, saúde, cultura, esporte, meio ambiente, inclusão social e desenvolvimento sustentável.

Segundo o padre Geraldo Gualandi, de 75 anos, fundador da creche, o recurso tornou o ambiente muito mais agradável para as crianças. Com turmas em período parcial e integral, funcionando das 7h às 17h, a nova área de lazer vai estimular, ainda mais, o desenvolvimento cognitivo, motor, afetivo e social dos matriculados, através das brincadeiras.

Um dos novos espaços da área de lazer da Creche Menino Jesus — Foto: Divulgação

“O impacto positivo é visível em nosso dia a dia. É a primeira vez que recebemos um parquinho com equipamentos totalmente novos. Para uma instituição filantrópica, que precisa dividir recursos entre alimentação, profissionais, estrutura, educação e outras despesas, receber esse incentivo do Sicoob significa antecipar melhorias, que levariam muito tempo para sair do papel”, destacou o padre.

Essa não foi a primeira vez que uma iniciativa ligada às obras sociais do padre Geraldo recebeu recursos do Edital Social do Sicoob. Atuando em diferentes frentes, como a Casa da Divina Providência, Orquestra e Musicalização, Escola Católica Santa Teresinha e Coleta Solidária, a instituição também recebeu apoio da cooperativa para a Associação dos Catadores, que desempenha um papel fundamental na preservação do meio ambiente.

“Com a doação recebida, impulsionamos o trabalho dos catadores, contratamos novos membros para a coleta de lixo reciclável, totalizando 20 funcionários atualmente, melhoramos o espaço onde é feita a separação do material e investimos na aquisição de um caminhão. As melhorias contribuem com o trabalho social e nos leva a cuidar da nossa cidade, recolhendo produtos que eram descartados na natureza, levando saúde, de forma geral, à população”, completou.

A Creche Menino Jesus atende mais de 200 crianças, de um a cinco anos de idade — Foto: Divulgação

O projeto, que começou de maneira discreta, atendendo crianças que viviam nas ruas e famílias que não tinham condições de garantir alimentação e cuidados básicos aos filhos, cresceu ao longo do tempo, se expandindo para diversas áreas da assistência social. Conhecido e reconhecido na região, o padre destaca a importância de parcerias, como a do Sicoob, para a continuidade das ações.

“Com o passar do tempo, ampliamos nossos projetos e, consequentemente, os custos para manter cada um deles. Durante toda minha trajetória religiosa, estive ligado ao cuidado de pessoas. E, neste mesmo caminho, encontrei parceiros, como o Sicoob, que também cuida de pessoas e, por isso, auxilia causas como essa”, concluiu.

As Obras Sociais do Padre Geraldo, iniciadas na década de 1980, concentram até hoje, trabalhos que combinam valores cristãos, convivência, responsabilidade, solidariedade e participação, fazendo a diferença na vida de centenas de famílias.

O Edital Social integra um conjunto de iniciativas desenvolvidas pelo sistema regional Sicoob ES voltadas à promoção da cidadania, da educação financeira, do cooperativismo e do desenvolvimento sustentável. Ao investir em organizações que já atuam nos territórios, a instituição busca ampliar o alcance de projetos locais e contribuir para o fortalecimento das comunidades onde está presente.

Nesta edição, o processo seletivo recebeu 592 projetos válidos, apresentados por 529 instituições de 96 municípios. As propostas passaram por análise técnica e foram avaliadas conforme critérios estabelecidos em regulamento, considerando aspectos como impacto social, viabilidade de execução, capacidade técnica das organizações e alinhamento com os objetivos da proposta. Ao final do processo, 272 projetos foram selecionados para receber apoio financeiro. Para conferir todas as informações, acesse o site .

Uma das agências do sistema regional Sicoob ES — Foto: Anderson Pires

Instituição financeira cooperativa, o Sicoob reúne mais de 10,2 milhões de cooperados e está presente em todos os estados brasileiros e no Distrito Federal. Oferece um portfólio completo de soluções financeiras, incluindo conta corrente, crédito, investimentos, cartões, previdência, consórcios, seguros, cobrança bancária e meios eletrônicos de pagamento. articles.title: Serralheiro morto por picada de formiga já teve reação alérgica | G1
articles.standfirst: Jorge Alves Lopes, de 61 anos, morava em Goiânia e foi para São João da Paraúna visitar o irmão. Ele foi socorrido até o pronto socorro da cidade, mas não resistiu.
articles.summary: Jorge Alves Lopes, de 61 anos, morava em Goiânia e foi para São João da Paraúna visitar o irmão.
articles.body:
O serralheiro Jorge Alves Lopes, de 61 anos, morreu após ser picado por formigas durante uma pescaria em São João da Paraúna , no oeste de Goiás. Morador de Goiânia , ele havia viajado para o município para visitar o irmão, Benedito dos Reis Lopes, que relatou que a vítima já havia sofrido uma reação alérgica anos antes. Jorge foi socorrido até o pronto socorro da cidade, mas não resistiu.

O episódio ocorreu no último sábado (10). Ao g1 , Benedito contou que Jorge havia chegado na noite de sexta-feira (9) para visitá-lo. Na manhã seguinte, os dois e um sobrinho foram pescar às margens do Rio Turvo.

A gente acredita que foram várias que atacaram ele. Isso já tinha acontecido com ele uma outra vez, já tinha muito tempo, mas ele era alérgico", explicou o irmão.

Jorge Alves Lopes, de 61 anos, morreu após ser picado por uma formiga, durante uma pescaria, em Goiás — Foto: Reprodução/ Perfil do Instagram de Jorge Alves Lopes

Segundo Benedito, a presença da formiga-de-fogo é comum na região onde estavam. Ele acredita que o irmão tenha sofrido múltiplas picadas, embora não saiba precisar quantas. "Lá, ele apresentou falta de ar e disse: 'Gente, parece que tá me tampando. Parece que tá me tampando!'. Aí, ele deu tipo um desmaio" , descreveu.

Diante do difícil acesso ao trecho do rio, Benedito e o sobrinho precisaram agir rápido para socorrer Jorge e encaminhá-lo à unidade de saúde do município. Conforme a família, a vítima já havia sido picada por formiga anos atrás, mas sem apresentar reação grave naquela oportunidade.

Bastante abalado, o pedreiro ressaltou o companheirismo entre eles, mesmo morando em cidades diferentes: "Nós sempre estávamos conversando um com o outro" . Jorge deixou um casal de filhos. Com a perda, restam cinco de nove irmãos.

articles.title: O movimento contra o voto feminino – no Brasil e no mundo - O Assunto #1823 | G1
articles.standfirst: Nas redes sociais, as vertentes mais extremas defendem até que o voto feminino deve ser proibido; em troca seria estabelecido o voto familiar, no qual o homem da casa decide.
articles.summary: Nas redes sociais, as vertentes mais extremas defendem até que o voto feminino deve ser proibido; em troca seria estabelecido o voto familiar, no qual o homem da casa decide.
articles.body:
Nos EUA, fazem sucesso entre grupos ultraconservadores conteúdos sobre onde supostamente deveria ser o lugar da mulher. Nas redes sociais, as vertentes mais extremas defendem até que o voto feminino deve ser proibido; em troca seria estabelecido o voto familiar, no qual o homem da casa decide e vai às urnas. Mais recentemente, esse movimento de caráter antifeminista vem encontrando eco também no Brasil, país onde as mulheres têm direito ao voto desde 1932 – nos EUA, o sufrágio universal já tem mais de um século. Nesta eleição, candidatos e candidatas conquistaram grande quantidade de votos – exatamente no mesmo pleito no qual o Congresso Nacional registra recorde de parlamentares mulheres.

Neste episódio, Natuza Nery tem duas convidadas. Primeiro, ela conversa com a professora de relações internacionais Tatiana Vargas Maia, que explica a origem e as motivações do movimento antifeminista que questiona o direito das mulheres ao voto. Depois, ela fala com a cientista política Marina Basso Lacerda sobre como este fenômeno se apresentou nas urnas brasileiras.

Convidadas: Tatiana Vargas Maia, professora de Relações Internacionais da UFRS, e Marina Basso Lacerda, doutora em ciência política e pesquisadora da USP e da UnB.

O podcast O Assunto é produzido por: Luiz Felipe Silva, Carlos Catelan, Luiz Gabriel Franco, Juliene Moretti, Stéphanie Nascimento, Marco Antônio Martins e Thomé Granemann. Na apresentação: Natuza Nery.

O Assunto é o podcast diário produzido pelo g1, disponível em todas as plataformas de áudio e no YouTube. Desde a estreia, em agosto de 2019, o podcast O Assunto soma mais de 168 milhões de downloads em todas as plataformas de áudio.

articles.title: Leripe Rádio Web é novo canal de comunicação da Prefeitura | G1
articles.standfirst: O canal também conta com o aplicativo para smartphone e desktop.
articles.summary: O canal também conta com o aplicativo para smartphone e desktop.
articles.body:
A Leripe Rádio Web vai ser mais um canal para divulgar ações, projetos e serviços da Administração Municipal direta e indireta — Foto: Divulgação

A Prefeitura de Rio das Ostras, por meio da Secretaria de Comunicação Social, inova e lança um novo canal que vai proporcionar uma maior interatividade entre a população e o Poder Público. Esse canal de Comunicação é a Leripe Rádio Web, que estará disponível nos sites e , da Fundação Rio das Ostras de Cultura.

O canal também conta com o aplicativo para smartphone e desktop que pode ser baixado pelo link . Os ouvintes poderão entrar em contato com a Rádio pelo número (22) 2771-6550 (somente WhatsApp) ou pelo e-mail jornalismo.riodasostras@gmail.com.

O objetivo é ampliar a divulgação das ações, projetos e serviços da Administração Pública, direta e indireta, desenvolvidos para o atendimento da população em uma plataforma digital de entretenimento. Além disso, também tem como finalidade atender, valorizar e prestigiar a classe artística local, que possui pouco espaço para apresentar seus trabalhos autorais, contribuir com ações promovidas pela Fundação Rio das Ostras de Cultura e de outras produções artístico-culturais desenvolvidas no Município.

A programação vai contar com uma seleção variada de ritmos, com artistas nacionais e internacionais consagrados, bem como talentos regionais que estejam despontando no cenário musical.

PÁGINA – A Rádio também conta com uma página própria dentro do site da Prefeitura ( ) com informações sobre a programação e os contatos para os ouvintes. Na página também ficarão disponíveis os programas criados para que as pessoas possam ouvir nos horários que quiserem.

PROGRAMAÇÃO – Com uma programação 24h por dia, a Leripe Rádio Web estreia com uma seleção musical de grandes artistas da Música Popular Brasileira, consagrados e talentos da Região, e programas produzidos pela equipe de comunicação da própria Secretaria. Dentre os programas que já estreiam neste lançamento estão o “Fala Cidadão”, que é um quadro que dá voz ao morador para que ele faça um questionamento ou elogio à Administração Municipal, com a devida resposta do gestor ligado ao tema. O objetivo é aproximar o cidadão do poder público. Outro programa é o “Minuto Cultural”, que apresenta curiosidades e informações sobre questões ligadas à cultura de uma forma geral.

Também estão previstos a criação de outros programas como um de entrevistas, com os gestores da Administração Municipal, podcasts com temas de interesse da população e a participação de representantes da sociedade civil organizada, agenda de eventos, um programa jornalístico com notícias da Cidade, da região, do Estado e do Mundo; e um programa esportivo.

ESCOLHA DO NOME – Leripe é um termo de origem tupi-guarani que significa “lugar de ostra”. Além disso, a palavra é o nome antigo do Município de Rio das Ostras. Também é uma forma de gerar um pertencimento entre o ouvinte e a Cidade, descaracterizando a rádio de um nome institucional formal.

articles.title: Trem descarrila no Paquistão e deixa ao menos 4 mortos | G1
articles.standfirst: Com 14 vagões, composição seguia de Karachi para Peshawar quando saiu dos trilhos; outras 30 pessoas ficaram feridas.
articles.summary: Com 14 vagões, composição seguia de Karachi para Peshawar quando saiu dos trilhos; outras 30 pessoas ficaram feridas.
articles.body:
Equipes fazem socorro de passageiros após trem descarrilar no Paquistão. — Foto: Rescue 1122 Emergency Department via AP

Um trem de passageiros descarrilou no início da manhã desta terça-feira no centro do Paquistão, deixando quatro mortos e 30 feridos, informaram a polícia e um porta-voz da Pakistan Railways.

O trem seguia da cidade portuária de Karachi, no sul do país, para Peshawar, no noroeste, quando saiu dos trilhos na cidade de Sher Shah, na província de Punjab, disse o porta-voz da ferrovia, Kaleem Akhtar.

Segundo ele, equipes de resgate retiraram os quatro corpos e retiraram os feridos dos 14 vagões do trem. As vítimas foram levadas para hospitais da região. Equipes de emergência e paramédicos foram mobilizados para o local.

O presidente Asif Ali Zardari e o primeiro-ministro Shehbaz Sharif manifestaram pesar em comunicados separados e pediram às autoridades que garantam o melhor atendimento médico possível aos feridos.

Acidentes ferroviários são relativamente comuns no Paquistão, onde o sistema ferroviário sofre há décadas com a falta de investimentos, trilhos obsoletos e sistemas de sinalização envelhecidos. Em 2023, dez vagões de um trem de passageiros descarrilaram no sul do país, matando 30 pessoas e deixando mais de 90 feridos.

Praia Fortaleza Ceará folga feriado sol — Foto: Divulgação

O próximo feriado nacional será em 2 de novembro, Dia de Finados. A data cairá em uma segunda-feira, o que permitirá três dias seguidos de descanso para os trabalhadores que folgam aos fins de semana.

Ao todo, ainda restam quatro feriados nacionais em 2026 . Além de Finados, outras datas podem formar fins de semana prolongados, dependendo do dia da semana em que caem e da possibilidade de emenda. (veja calendário abaixo)

Nem todos os trabalhadores são dispensados nos feriados . A legislação permite o funcionamento de atividades consideradas essenciais e de outras categorias autorizadas a trabalhar nessas datas.

⚠️ Nesses casos, quem trabalha no feriado pode ter direito a remuneração em dobro ou a uma folga compensatória, conforme as regras aplicáveis.

Ao todo, 2026 terá 10 feriados nacionais, sendo que 9 cairão em dias úteis. O calendário é favorável para quem deseja planejar folgas prolongadas ao longo do ano.

O mês de novembro terá três feriados. Depois do dia 2, a próxima data será 15 de novembro , quando é celebrada a Proclamação da República. O feriado cairá em um domingo e, por isso, não haverá possibilidade de emenda.

articles.title: 'Deu pena', diz moradora que vive em barraca após cheia no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Moradores de Uruguaiana improvisaram estruturas perto das residências atingidas pela água. Quase 500 pessoas estão fora de casa na Fronteira Oeste.
articles.summary: Moradores de Uruguaiana improvisaram estruturas perto das residências atingidas pela água. Quase 500 pessoas estão fora de casa na Fronteira Oeste.
articles.body:
Eva Maria Farias Morando mora temporariamente em uma barraca após fortes chuvas — Foto: Reprodução/ RBS TV

Morando temporariamente em uma barraca com uma das filhas e cinco netos , a aposentada Eva Maria Farias acompanha de perto os impactos da cheia do Rio Uruguai em sua casa, em Uruguaiana .

“Hoje mesmo de manhã eu fui lá ver minha casa, me deu pena", diz Eva.

A água chegou a quase um metro de profundidade na residência da família.

Eva diz que prefere permanecer na barraca em vez de ir para um abrigo, tanto pela privacidade quanto pela proximidade da residência. No local, a família precisou reorganizar a rotina enquanto espera a água baixar.

Na mesma esquina, Rosa Maria Minho Viana também vive em uma barraca perto de casa. Ela mora na região praticamente desde que nasceu e convive há anos com as enchentes.

“Eu mesma que montei”, conta Rosa sobre a barraca onde vive durante a cheia em Uruguaiana.

Na barraca, ela fica com o filho , que precisa de acompanhamento constante. A filha, o genro e um neto estão em outra estrutura, onde a família prepara as refeições.

Uruguaiana durante cheias do Rio Uruguai — Foto: Reprodução/ RBS TV

Outros moradores atingidos pela cheia deixaram completamente as proximidades das residências. É o caso da família de Rosicler Soares da Silva, que está em um abrigo desde 6 de outubro.

Rosicler está com o marido e as três filhas . As mais novas, as gêmeas Julia e Maria Antônia, têm três meses e nasceram prematuras, com 32 semanas. Esta é a segunda inundação deste ano que obriga a família a sair de casa.

Gêmeas Julia e Maria Antônia — Foto: Reprodução/ RBS TV

Mesmo com a mudança de rotina, a mãe conta que as bebês conseguem manter o sono durante a noite:

"Elas dormem a noite toda, só acordam o horário que têm que mamar".

Na casa da família, a água está a pouco menos de um metro de profundidade .

Quase 500 pessoas estão fora de casa na Fronteira Oeste em razão das cheias. Em Uruguaiana, o Rio Uruguai está 1,30 metro acima da cota de inundação .

Segundo o Serviço Geológico do Brasil, o nível do Rio Uruguai deve continuar subindo nas próximas horas em São Borja, Itaqui e Uruguaiana.

O alerta vermelho da Defesa Civil estadual para inundações na região segue até terça-feira (13).

articles.title: Bumble shares soar after report dating firm in $1bn takeover talks
articles.summary: The jump pushed Bumble's stock market valuation to more than $580m but that is still far below their peak of more than $14bn.
articles.body:
Shares in dating app company Bumble soared by almost 50% on Monday after a report that it is in advanced talks to be bought for around $1bn (£757m).

Technology holding company Ithaca could announce a deal to buy the Texas-based firm as early as this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.

The jump in Bumble's shares pushed its stock market valuation to over $580m but that is still far below a peak of more than $14bn it reached after listing on the Nasdaq in 2021 .

Bumble is one of the world's most downloaded dating apps, operating in a crowded market where growth has slowed. The BBC has contacted Bumble and Ithaca for comment.

Bumble was launched in 2014 by Whitney Wolfe Herd, who was also a co-founder of dating app giant Tinder.

Wolfe Herd built Bumble's brand around a distinctive feature that only allowed women to initiate conversations with matches.

It recently abandoned that rule , prompting debate among users over whether the app had lost what set it apart from rivals.

"Today, our community is asking for more flexibility, less pressure, and more opportunities to create real, meaningful connections and that is what this new experience provides," Wolfe Herd said in August.

Dating apps like Bumble have come under pressure in recent years as some younger users have grown disillusioned with browsing for dates.

Bumble said in 2025 that it would cut almost a third of its workforce as the industry grappled with what Wolfe Herd described as an "inflection point" in online dating.

Investments in other dating companies have also soured as apps have struggled to convince users to pay for their services.

Match Group - which owns apps including Tinder, OkCupid and Hinge - has also seen its shares fall sharply from their peak in 2021.

According a report by media watchdog Ofcom in 2025, adults in the UK were spending less time on dating apps compared to three years earlier.

Some single people are instead turning to board game get-togethers , book clubs and other group activities in the hope of finding a partner.

articles.title: 'Mar gaya,mar gaya tera bhai': 'Punched in chest', how row over metro seat turned deadly in Delhi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: “Mar gaya, mar gaya tera bhai gir gaya” (He is dead, your brother has fallen down).
articles.body: NEW DELHI: “Mar gaya, mar gaya tera bhai gir gaya” (He is dead, your brother has fallen down). These were the words Durga Sharma kept repeating over the phone to her younger son, Deepak (45), after his elder brother, Pawan Sharma, became unconscious following an altercation with a father-son duo over seats reserved for senior citizens on a Delhi Metro train on Oct 8.Pawan’s family had been planning to celebrate his 49th birthday on Nov 2, with Deepak preparing a surprise for his elder brother. Instead, the family is now grappling with his death, which Deepak alleges followed an argument with the two men.Row over seats reserved for senior citizensOn Oct 8, Pawan and his mother, Durga (65), were returning to their Yamuna Vihar home after visiting Deepak, who was unwell, in Gurgaon.Sanjay Pratap Singh, a retired IAS officer, and his son, Sidharth Singh, both residents of Noida, boarded the train at Mandi House. According to police, an argument broke out over the seats where Pawan and his mother were sitting.According to Durga, the two rudely asked them to vacate their seats. “We got up, and my son told them they could now lie down on the seats. The older man grabbed Pawan by the collar and slapped him. When he objected, the man’s son assaulted him. When I tried to intervene, the older man restrained me,” she said.Deepak said his brother had already given up the seat but was still subjected to rude remarks. “My brother had given up the seat but was still subjected to rude remarks by the other party.”‘He had already died by the time I reached’When the train reached Supreme Court metro station around 5.47 pm, Pawan became unconscious, police said. He was rushed to LNJP Hospital, where he was declared dead.Deepak said he called his mother back after hearing her distressed voice on the phone. She told him she was taking Pawan to hospital in an ambulance. He then spoke to the ambulance staff, who asked him to reach the hospital.Pawan was no more by the time Deepak arrived. “My mother was fainting. The hospital staff did not tell her, but when I reached there, I was told that he had already died,” he said.Deepak alleged that his brother had been punched in the chest during the altercation. “Pawan was not an aggressive person. He was a family man and never fought with anyone.”Family loses sole breadwinnerPawan’s death has left his wife and two children without their primary financial support. His 19-year-old son is in the first year of college, while his 15-year-old daughter studies in Class X. Pawan worked as a clerk and was the sole breadwinner for the family.After their father’s death, Pawan had taken responsibility for the household, becoming the family’s main support. He had hoped to give his children a better future, Deepak said. “But now, everything is over.”Father-son duo arrestedPolice recorded Durga’s statement and registered a case against the father-son duo under Sections 105 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to culpable homicide not amounting to murder and acts committed with common intention.Both men were arrested based on evidence collected during the investigation and remanded to 14 days of judicial custody.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Patagonia reported $180 million in payments to its environmental owner since 2022, according to a November 2025 report
articles.summary: In September 2022, Patagonia founder Yvon Chouinard announced a new ownership structure intended to direct the outdoor clothing company’s excess profits
articles.body: In September 2022, Patagonia founder Yvon Chouinard announced a new ownership structure intended to direct the outdoor clothing company’s excess profits towards environmental work while protecting its values. In November 2025, Patagonia published its Work in Progress Report, detailing payments to its environmental owner alongside shortcomings in the company’s own operations. Released on 12 November 2025, Patagonia’s Work in Progress Report says the company had paid $180 million to the Holdfast Collective since the ownership change in 2022. The nonprofit owns 98% of Patagonia, while the Patagonia Purpose Trust holds the remaining 2% and all voting stock. The money comes from excess profits, meaning funds left after the business reinvests in its operations and sets aside reserves for unforeseen events. Patagonia remains a for-profit company and continues to donate 1% of sales to grassroots environmental groups. Its report also details emissions, products without end-of-life solutions and unresolved supply-chain challenges, offering a picture of an experiment that remains unfinished.Patagonia ownership structure explained: how the Holdfast Collective and the Patagonia Purpose Trust own the companyThe ownership change was announced in Chouinard’s letter, Earth is now our only shareholder, published on 14 September 2022. The phrase described the company’s purpose rather than a literal transfer of shares to the planet. Patagonia’s voting stock went to the Patagonia Purpose Trust, which owns 2% of the company, while all nonvoting stock went to the Holdfast Collective, which owns 98%. The distinction is important. Nonvoting stock carries economic value but no decision-making authority. The Patagonia Purpose Trust was established to protect the company’s mission and oversee decisions affecting its values. Patagonia’s ownership structure gives the trust control through its voting shares, while the Holdfast Collective holds the nonvoting shares. The trust’s role is therefore distinct from Holdfast’s role in receiving dividends for environmental work. Holdfast Collective, meanwhile, is a 501(c)(4) nonprofit that can make grants and investments and advocate for causes and political candidates.Chouinard said the family rejected a conventional sale because a new owner might not preserve Patagonia’s values or protect its workforce. He also criticised the pressure public companies face to prioritise short-term financial returns. The new structure was designed to keep the company operating as a business while directing its excess profits towards environmental work. Patagonia has not become a charity. It remains a for-profit company, a certified B Corp and a California benefit corporation. Its commitment to donate 1% of sales to grassroots environmental organisations, which began in 1985, is now embedded in its charter. Chief executive Ryan Gellert and the leadership team continue to run the business under the board’s direction, while the Purpose Trust provides additional oversight of its mission.Patagonia Holdfast Collective dividends: how $180 million has moved towards environmental work since 2022The dividend connects Patagonia’s commercial performance to its environmental commitments. Under the ownership structure described on the company’s ownership page, excess profits are distributed to Holdfast Collective after the business has reinvested in itself and accounted for reserves, including money set aside for unforeseen events such as a pandemic. Patagonia’s Work in Progress Report, published in November 2025, reports $180 million in cumulative payments to the Holdfast Collective since the 2022 ownership transfer. The figure records payments reported by Patagonia; it does not, by itself, establish the environmental outcomes achieved with the money. Holdfast Collective says it will use the funds to fight the environmental crisis, protect nature and biodiversity, and support communities.The report gives a specific example of how the funding has been used. In June 2025, Holdfast Collective contributed $2 million towards The Conservation Fund’s purchase and protection of 8,000 acres near Georgia’s Okefenokee Swamp, the largest black-water swamp in the United States. The purchase was intended to help protect the area from the threat of mining.This funding is separate from Patagonia’s longstanding 1% of sales pledge. In fiscal year 2025, the company reported $14.7 million in grants and in-kind support for 824 nonprofits through its 1% for the Planet programme. It also reported $240 million in cumulative environmental grants since the company was founded. Its Patagonia Action Works platform generated more than 1 million actions in support of grantees during the same fiscal year, including donations, petition signatures and participation in events. These figures describe different forms of support: dividends to Holdfast Collective, grants and in-kind assistance through the 1% programme, and actions facilitated through the company’s platform. They should not be treated as interchangeable measures of spending or impact.Patagonia Work in Progress Report: what the company admits about emissions, repairs and products without a recycling planThe report does not portray Patagonia as having solved the environmental problems associated with making and selling clothing. Chouinard acknowledges that the company’s work and donations remain insufficient, while Gellert describes a fundamental tension: making products requires resources, even when those products are designed to last. Patagonia reported 182,646 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions in fiscal year 2025. It repaired 174,799 products worldwide during that period, but approximately 85% of its products still lacked an end-of-life solution. The latter figure highlights a persistent challenge for a company that promotes durability and repair: extending a product’s useful life does not automatically resolve what happens when it can no longer be used.The company also abandoned its goal of carbon neutrality by 2025, concluding that carbon neutrality achieved through offsets did not meet its standards for addressing its environmental impact. On chemicals, the report says that, as of 2025, 100% of new products were made without intentionally added PFAS. This is a claim about the company’s new products and intentional use, not a statement that every existing product or every part of its supply chain is entirely free of these substances. Patagonia’s report includes critical reactions to its approach, including accusations of virtue signalling and calls for the company to concentrate on selling clothes. The inclusion of criticism reflects the report’s attempt to address scepticism, although the document remains a company-produced account of its own performance.In his letter accompanying the report, Chouinard says the 2022 transfer resolved how Patagonia’s values could be protected beyond his lifetime and created a way to direct more money towards environmental work. He also points to trade wars and an assault on nature as challenges facing that work. Gellert describes the report as a means of accountability rather than self-congratulation. The $180 million figure demonstrates the scale of the funding Patagonia says it has directed to Holdfast Collective since 2022. The emissions, repair and product-disposal figures show why the company’s environmental record cannot be assessed by its donations alone. Its ownership model establishes a mechanism for directing profits towards conservation, but the report also acknowledges the unresolved consequences of manufacturing and selling products. Whether the structure delivers lasting environmental benefits will depend not only on the money transferred, but also on how effectively that money is used and how much Patagonia reduces the harm associated with its own business.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A series of missile and drone attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels has raised concerns over Saudi Arabia’s ability to protect its critical infrastructure,
articles.body: A series of missile and drone attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels has raised concerns over Saudi Arabia’s ability to protect its critical infrastructure, with a strike on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 10 killing 13 people and injuring more than 300, according to Saudi authorities.According to Forbes analysis, Saudi Arabia has struggled to contain the Houthis despite spending approximately $83 billion on defence in 2025.Saudi Arabia’s military arsenal includes F-15 fighter jets, Eurofighter Typhoons and advanced Patriot and THAAD missile defence systems. However, its struggle to prevent repeated Houthi attacks highlights the gap between possessing sophisticated military hardware and effectively deploying it to protect critical infrastructure.The challenge is compounded by the Houthis’ use of missiles and drones, which can force Saudi Arabia to expend costly interception systems against comparatively inexpensive incoming weapons.Why Saudi Arabia is strugglingThe Forbes analysis identifies weaknesses in coordination within the kingdom’s security establishment, arguing that divisions between military and security institutions can hamper intelligence-sharing and operational effectiveness.Another major challenge is the asymmetric nature of the conflict. The Houthis can use relatively inexpensive drones and missiles to threaten airports and other strategic infrastructure, forcing Saudi Arabia to maintain costly air-defence systems on constant alert. Even when incoming weapons are intercepted, repeated attacks can impose financial costs and sustain pressure on the kingdom’s security apparatus.The Houthis’ growing military capabilities also complicate Saudi Arabia’s response. Their experience in Yemen’s prolonged conflict, combined with access to missile technology and alleged Iranian assistance, has enabled them to threaten targets beyond the territory they control.Saudi Arabia’s superior conventional arsenal does not automatically eliminate this threat, particularly when the Houthis rely on dispersed operations and repeated strikes rather than conventional battlefield engagements.Regional division and disagreement between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates over Yemen have weakened coordination among forces opposed to the Houthis, complicating efforts to contain the group through a unified military campaign.You use AI every day. articles.title: Man rescued after being trapped in Sardinian cave for 26 hours
articles.summary: The 31-year-old cave expert was found alive, 32ft underground, after more than 100 emergency personnel worked to free him.
articles.body:
A man has been rescued from a cave in Sardinia, Italy, after being trapped about 32ft (10 metres) underground for about 26 hours following a rockfall.

The 31-year-old, Luca Olmetto, was inside Gorropeddu cave at Urzulei, a town on the Italian island, when he became stuck on Sunday, according to ANSA, a local news agency.

Following a major rescue operation, involving more than 100 emergency personnel working meticulously over 24 hours, Olmetto was found alive and freed on Monday afternoon, the National Alpine and Speleological Rescue Corps said.

Olmetto, who studies caves, was then airlifted to hospital for further medical checks and treatment, local media said.

He had been exploring the cave, which is situated along a mountain range in central-eastern Sardinia, when rock suddenly collapsed on Sunday afternoon.

A rescue operation then followed, led by the National Alpine and Speleological Rescue Corps and the local fire department.

It was a "particularly complex operation", the National Alpine and Speleological Rescue Corps said in a statement shared on social media along with pictures of the team working in what they described as "extremely confined" spaces.

After gently and manually removing debris to access the cavity of the cave, the man was brought to the surface, the statement said.

The speleologist was then stabilised and transferred by helicopter to the hospital, it said.

In a post shared on social media, the council of Codrongianos, a town in north-west Sardinia where Olmetto is from, said: "After hours of great anxiety, the news that the entire Codrongianos was waiting for has finally arrived: Luca is out of the cave!

"It has been a difficult hour, during which the entire community has been on edge following the rescue operations," the post continued.

The council of Codrongianos thanked the rescuers "who worked tirelessly to reach him".

articles.title: BBC shelves plans for new Archers studio as part of cost-cutting
articles.summary: The drama has been recording in Birmingham for 75 years, making it the world's longest running soap opera.
articles.body:
The BBC has shelved plans to build a new bespoke studio for The Archers in Birmingham as part of its wider drive to cut costs, opening up the possibility it could be recorded outside of the city for the first time.

The world's longest-running soap opera, The Archers has been recording in the West Midlands city for 75 years.

The BBC had initially pledged to build the show a new studio in the Tea Factory, the corporation's new hub in Digbeth, central Birmingham.

The broadcaster said it was "currently assessing the BBC's existing studio facilities around the UK as well as other external studio options in the West Midlands".

"We recognise and value The Archers' long-standing relationship with the West Midlands, which remains an important part of the programme's future," the statement added.

The BBC Radio 4 drama, set in the fictional West Midlands village of Ambridge, first aired nationally on 1 January 1951. It celebrated its 75th anniversary earlier this year.

Mayor of the West Midlands Richard Parker said he was "very disappointed by news that the BBC plans to move its production out of the city".

"The Archers was born in Birmingham and is a key part of our broadcasting heritage," he wrote in a statement shared to Facebook.

"We have the talent and the facilities here. There is no good reason why we should lose a programme that has called Birmingham home for decades."

Parker said he would meet Director General Matt Brittin later this week to "discuss every available option" to keep The Archers in Birmingham.

"The BBC promised to invest and support our regions, this is entirely the opposite of that," he said.

A spokesperson for the BBC said they were looking to find a solution that would "deliver significant savings whilst also maintaining The Archers' high production standards."

They confirmed that the series' production team is still set to move "as planned" to Digbeth in early 2028, but, "after careful consideration", they would no longer be building a new recording studio in the Tea Factory.

The statement also noted that The Archer's recording schedule meant cast members are in the studio approximately eight days a month, with many actors travelling to the recordings as they live in locations across the UK.

"The impact on the cast will be fully considered as part of our assessment process," the spokesperson said, emphasising that "no final decision has been made".

Videos show passengers being helped out of the stationary coaster cars and onto a staircase. Cobb County Police said detectives from the department’s major crimes unit were investigating.In a statement, Six Flags said it was “deeply saddened by the guest incident” and that park staff and local authorities had responded immediately. articles.title: Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC
articles.summary: In his first interview since being forced from his post, Gen Syrskyi speaks about Ukraine's future in the war.
articles.body:
Ukraine has stabilised the front line and "broken Russia's ability to advance" by killing so many of its men, Ukraine's former commander-in-chief has said in an interview with the BBC.

Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi made the comments in an exclusive interview, his first since he was dramatically forced from his post in the summer.

He addressed his sacking, disagreeing with his critics who declared him too "old school" to command Ukraine's new, technologically advanced forces.

He also pushed back against allegations made by soldiers who previously served under him, who told the BBC they were ordered to remain at their positions even when they were almost surrounded by Russians, leading to high losses.

Syrskyi said that Moscow's overall losses in the war were six times higher than Ukraine's. "If you count only dead, then it's up to 11 times," he added.

Neither Russia nor Ukraine officially release the numbers of their dead. Ukraine's military says it inflicted record losses this year on Russian soldiers in September, although that cannot be verified.

UK intelligence chiefs estimate Russia has lost around half a million men killed in Ukraine since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022. The US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies meanwhile believes Ukraine has lost up to 150,000 troops killed by June 2026.

He says this difference in death toll – as well as technological advances, and a strategy of attacking weak points in Russia's lines while containing their advances in other parts – accounts for the current stalemate at the front.

In the first six months of 2026, Russia managed overall to seize 61 sq km, the general said. "It's an indication that the front line has been stabilised."

The Institute for Study of War (ISW) has also confirmed this trend. One of its recent reports says that in September 2026, Moscow lost more territory than it took.

Syrskyi was appointed Ukraine's commander-in-chief in 2024. He had previously won praise for defending Kyiv at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, and for leading the successful counteroffensive east of Kharkiv in the autumn of that year.

But President Volodymyr Zelensky fired Syrskyi this summer, amid a major disagreement with then-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Fedorov had said that instead of adapting to the realities of the changing war, the army under Syrskyi had blocked his initiatives.

Zelensky initially fired Fedorov, as tensions burst into the open between the two men. But mass street protests then forced the president to also fire Syrskyi, replacing him with Maj Gen Mykhailo Drapatyi, 43.

Syrskyi told the BBC that he had "disagreements" with Fedorov because the latter "didn't take into consideration the interests of the army" when procuring weapons and supplies.

Fedorov had created an "imbalance" in supplies, Syrskyi said. He had prioritised drones while overlooking key front-line kit such as unmanned ground vehicles, pick-up trucks and motorbikes. Even with drones, Syrskyi said, there were shortages as the army got only half of what they needed.

Fedorov was a popular young minister who was known for his digital and technological initiatives. Many contrasted him with Syrskyi, who critics thought was not fit to lead the new technological arms race with Russia.

But Syrskyi disagrees with such criticism. It was during his time the use of drones reached this new, unprecedented level, including deep strikes more than 2,000km (1,200 miles) behind enemy lines, he said. Ukraine was the first country to create the Unmanned Systems Forces as a separate branch of armed forces, under his command: now, he said, drones account for 80% of Russia's losses.

Under his military leadership, however, Ukrainian troops undertook chaotic withdrawals from the eastern cities of Avdiivka and Vuhledar, and from around Pokrovsk.

Soldiers who spoke to the BBC in the past complained that they were ordered to remain at their positions at any costs. By the time they were told to pull back, it was often too late as they were almost surrounded by Russian troops.

Syrskyi does not deny that such situations occur on the front line. But he told the BBC that Ukraine was fighting against a far more powerful army.

In 2025, the ratio of jets and bombs was 18 to one in Moscow's favour, he said. In the same year, Russia had two-and-a-half times more artillery pieces and shells than Ukraine. And with four million militarily trained men who they can mobilise, Russian forces can create chances to push through, he argued.

One of Syrskyi's most famous operations was an incursion into Russia's Kursk region that started in August 2024. It ended with a dramatic retreat the following spring, which some soldiers described as "catastrophic". Syrskyi, however, insisted that the Kursk operation was "a necessity".

"In the summer 2024, Russian forces were pushing along all main directions on the front line with up to six times more troops than we had," he explained.

The Kursk incursion disrupted Russia's offensive and forced Moscow to redirect troops, giving Ukraine a respite and a chance for its stretched brigades in the east and south to recover, Syrskyi said.

He also had strong words for European allies who doubt that Russia may have territorial ambitions beyond Ukraine. He advised European partners to start preparing for the war now and "drop all illusions that [it] will not come".

He also said he believed Ukraine's war was going to become even more technological. There will be more robots, automated systems and artificial intelligence (AI). "Even ordinary weapons now get an AI-based control system to enhance their capabilities," he said.

Such technologies can give a new life to conventional weapons like tanks. Both Russia and Ukraine were now racing to develop "active systems of defence" to protect armoured vehicles, Syrskyi said.

But he insisted that "the human role will remain definitive [on the battlefield] because [people] will need to control those systems".
